parts:
Thanks Maarten for getting back on this. I am testing Renijn in a maven class where I provide the dependencies in pom.xml file as:

<!-- REnjin Dependency(Testing) -->

<dependency>

<groupId>org.renjin.cran</groupId>

<artifactId>signal</artifactId>

<version>0.7-6-b18</version>

<scope>provided</scope>

</dependency>

<dependency>

<groupId>org.renjin</groupId>

<artifactId>renjin-script-engine</artifactId>

<version>0.8.2005</version>

<scope>provided</scope>

</dependency>

<dependency>

<groupId>org.renjin.cran</groupId>

<artifactId>exptest</artifactId>

<version>1.2-b214</version>

<scope>provided</scope>

</dependency>

</dependencies>

<repositories>

<repository>

<id>bedatadriven</id>

<name>bedatadriven public repo</name>

<url>http://nexus.bedatadriven.com/content/groups/public/</url>

</repository>

</repositories>

Also while executing I provide the dependency in the classpath. Generally all other dependencies are found at runtime but Renjin's dependency are missing while executing.

On Tue, May 10, 2016 at 2:05 PM, Kallen, Maarten-Jan <m...@bedatadriven.com> wrote:

Without knowing more about your setup and how you manage dependencies, there is nothing we can do to help you. If you use Maven and follow the instructions on the website, then Maven should take care of things for you. If you are managing dependencies manually then you should look in the pom.xml file of the Renjin Script Engine to find it's dependencies: https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/master/script-engine/pom.xml

Regards

Maarten-Jan

messages.author: c6f33a2b75082d5e
messages.subject: Re: Fwd: How can I get Renjin dependency jar
parts: You have specified the scope of renjin-script-engine as "provided". This tells maven that YOU are providing the depende

messages.author: c6f33a2b75082d5e
messages.subject: Re: Fwd: How can I get Renjin dependency jar
parts:
Sorry, responding from cell phone, with bad touch screen.


You have specified a scope of "provided" which means that you are providing the dependency at runtime and maven needn't bother.

This is probably not what you want.
